articles.title: Home Assistant protects unfinished edits when you go back
articles.dek: Back gestures ask before discarding an automation, while leaving a live scene restores the devices it changed.
body: An accidental swipe back no longer has to mean rebuilding an automation. Home Assistant’s automation, script and scene editors ask before abandoning unsaved changes when someone uses Android’s back gesture, the browser Back button or Alt+Left. Declining keeps the editor open; confirming leaves in the same step.

Leaving the scene editor also restores the devices’ earlier states after live editing. Previously, using the sidebar or switching scenes could leave the home in the temporary preview. Putting the browser tab in the background does not end live mode.

Petar Petrov extends the safeguards he added in August for navigation through the quick bar, editor links and companion-app commands. The raw dashboard YAML editor gains the same unsaved-changes protection, closing another route to losing work.

articles.title: Overcast connects to Music Assistant without a password
articles.dek: A QR code opens setup to listeners whose Overcast accounts exist only in the app.
body: Overcast listeners who never created a password get a way to connect their existing account to Music Assistant. Setup displays a QR code to scan with an iPhone camera; approving the request in Overcast lets Music Assistant pick up the session.

The original setup required an email address and password, excluding accounts created only in the app. Those credentials remain an alternative for people who have them. If an app-authorized session expires, the error points back to setup instead of asking for a password the account never had.
OzGav adds the sign-in flow, with approval from Marvin Schenkel. Subscriptions and listening progress still flow one way into Music Assistant: playback there does not update the Overcast account.

pullRequests.title: Sign in to Overcast with a QR code instead of a password

articles.title: EnergyZero adds quarter-hour electricity prices to Home Assistant
articles.dek: Existing price sensors gain 15-minute detail, with hourly readings remaining the default.
body: Households following EnergyZero electricity prices get a choice between hourly and quarter-hourly readings in Home Assistant. The setting applies to today’s and tomorrow’s price data and the existing electricity sensors; the next-price reading follows the selected one-hour or 15-minute interval.

Changing the option reloads the integration automatically and preserves existing entity IDs. A related correction renames the sensor that counts cheaper or equally priced periods and removes its misleading hours unit. Templates or cards that depend on that unit need adjustment; comparisons using only the number do not.

This changes the detail of the price data, not how frequently Home Assistant checks for updates. Gas readings are unaffected, and the separate action for fetching energy prices still returns hourly values. Klaas Schoute contributes the feature, with approval from silamon.

articles.title: ESPHome fixes brightness commands that change a light’s color
articles.dek: Lights connected through MQTT keep their white level separate from overall brightness when a scene sets both.
body: A lighting scene can look wrong when a command changes color and brightness together. ESPHome restores the information Home Assistant needs to dim compatible lights independently of their color channels when they communicate through MQTT, a messaging protocol used to connect devices.

Missing brightness information made Home Assistant scale the color values instead of sending a separate brightness setting. On lights with red, green, blue and white channels, that could change the white level while leaving overall brightness untouched. Ryan Ronnander reports verifying the correction on 17 BK7231T-based lights.
This is Ronnander’s first contribution to ESPHome, with review and approval from Jesse Hills.

pullRequests.title: [mqtt] Restore brightness flag in light discovery

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps Google Drive backups visible after a bad description
articles.dek: One edited file no longer breaks the entire backup list and its sensors.
body: Editing or clearing a backup file’s description in Google Drive could take down Home Assistant’s backup listing and every associated sensor. The integration skips unreadable records with a warning, keeping the rest of the collection visible. It does not repair the description of a skipped backup.
The change also keeps files in Drive’s trash out of backup lookups and stops upload progress from moving backwards after a retry. tronikos contributes the fixes, with approval from zweckj.

pullRequests.title: Make Google Drive backup listing resilient to unreadable metadata

articles.title: Music Assistant brings speakers back after an announcement
articles.dek: A grouping fix stops an interrupted speaker from getting stranded outside the music it was playing with others.
body: An announcement on a synchronized Music Assistant speaker could detach it from its group and leave it unable to rejoin, even manually. The grouping check no longer mistakes a speaker playing on its own for the leader of another active group.
Marvin Schenkel reproduced the failure with two Sendspin clients and verified that the group restores automatically after the announcement with the fix.

pullRequests.title: Fix players not regrouping after an announcement on a synced player
